name: The Messiah: Prophet, Priest, and King

objectives.text: Identify Jesus as the King promised in the Bible who rules over all things
Describe a priest as someone who goes to God on behalf of the people and prays for them
Recall that a prophet is someone God sends to speak His words to people
Retell how Samuel anointed David with oil to show that God had chosen him to be king
Explain that the Hebrew word Messiah and the Greek word Christ both mean Anointed One
Identify the three offices of prophet, priest, and king that the Reformed tradition confesses Jesus fulfills
Explain how Jesus does the work of a prophet by revealing God and His will through His teaching
Explain how Jesus does the work of a priest by standing before God for His people and interceding for them
Explain how Jesus does the work of a king by ruling, protecting, and defending His people and conquering His enemies
Summarize key Old Testament promises of a coming prophet, priest, and king
Compare Moses as prophet, Aaron as priest, and David as king with Jesus, noting both likenesses and the ways Jesus is greater
Explain how Peter applies the promise of a prophet like Moses to Jesus in his sermon in Acts
Analyze the anointing of prophets, priests, and kings in the Old Testament and what the anointing signified
Explain how Jesus' anointing with the Spirit at His baptism and His reading of Isaiah 61 in Nazareth mark Him as the Anointed One
Analyze why the offices of priest and king were kept separate in Israel and how the prophets anticipated their union in one person
Connect the priest-king Melchizedek to the eternal priesthood of Jesus as Hebrews explains it
Interpret Jesus' high priestly prayer as an example of His intercession for His people
Explain the kingship of Christ over the nations and all creation from the Psalms and the New Testament
Distinguish the political messianic expectations of Jesus' day from the kingdom Jesus proclaimed
Construct a profile of the threefold office of Christ using Scripture and the Reformed confessions
Analyze how the Reformed tradition relates each office of Christ to a human need, such as ignorance, guilt, and bondage
Evaluate how the church is described as sharing in Christ's anointing as prophets, priests, and kings
Defend from Hebrews and Revelation the claim that Jesus is the final Word, the final High Priest, and the final King
Evaluate views that present Jesus in only one office, such as a moral teacher alone, against the biblical portrait of the Messiah
Write a synthesis tracing the offices of prophet, priest, and king from the Old Testament to their fulfillment in Christ

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies: King, priest, prophet, Messiah meaning, the three offices, Jesus as Prophet, the Moses and David comparison, OT anointing, John 17, Melchizedek, Kingship over the nations, the threefold office profile, the church's share in the offices, final Word and Authority, and the OT synthesis. Merged the Christ as Greek word item into the Messiah meaning objective. Replaced the vague observe item with identifying the three offices. Recast final Sacrifice as final High Priest so atonement stays with the Sacrifice and Atonement sibling. Added parallel priest and king work objectives keyed to WSC Q24-26. Added new objectives on David's anointing, OT messianic promises, Acts 3 and Deuteronomy 18, Jesus' Spirit anointing and Luke 4, the separation and promised union of priest and king, first-century political expectations, how each office meets a human need, and one-office distortions. Added confessional anchors from WCF 8.1, WLC Q42-45, and HC Q32.
